newsitem.title: CHINA: SHANGHAI COPPER FUTURES END DOWN IN SLOW TRADING.
newsitem.headline: SHANGHAI COPPER FUTURES END DOWN IN SLOW TRADING.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly down in slow trade on Wednesday on speculative selling from retail investors, as copper on the London Metal Exchange (LME) consolidated in a narrow range overnight, traders said.
LME copper appeared set to break out of the $2,260/70 to $2,320/30 band, but failed to trigger the expected sell-stops in the mid-$2,250s.
Three months ended at $2,278, up $4 a tonne. London analysts saw it remaining vulnerable on Wednesday, with support at $2,255 and resistance at $2,300 per tonne.
In Shanghai, the most actively traded December 1997 contract ended at 21,210 yuan ($2,558) per tonne, losing 90 yuan. It opened at an intraday high of 21,280 and hit a low of 21,200 yuan.
August fell 50 yuan to 20,750, September 10 to 20,890, October 30 to 21,150, November 40 to 21,230 and the January 1997 contract, the only rising contract, put on 10 to 21,250 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 25,870 tonnes from 32,310 tonnes.
Copper opened mostly lower and moved in a very narrow range for most of the session.
Traders said many institutional investors remained on the sidelines due to uncertain short-term direction.
"Some speculative selling from retail investors was responsible for today's losses but volume continued to drop, indicating downward potential will be limited in the short term," one trader said.
"Copper will move in a narrow range in the next few days and wait for fresh market-moving news," he added.
"Copper is likely to move around the 21,000-yuan level in the next few days," a second trader said.
In Shanghai, physical copper prices closed around 20,750-yuan level, down from 20,800 yuan per tonne at the opening session due to weak market sentiment on the futures market.
Aluminium ended down on profit-taking. August fell 30 to 14,520 yuan per tonne, September 50 to 14,750, October 130 to 14,820, November 120 to 14,980 and December 230 to 15,050 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 2,810 tonnes from 5,320 tonnes.
